BRING YOUR OWN GROOVE

MIDI + backing audio.

Load a MIDI drum part and its matching recording. Save on this device for local practice, or sign in as a teacher and choose Publish to school to share the files and sync settings with every student.

No MIDI selected

1. Select the drum parts

Other instruments stay out of your score.

2. Check the drum assignments

These are separate from your keyboard keys.

3. Add backing audio optional

Optional · MP3, WAV, or another browser-supported audio file

Positive offsets delay the recording; negative offsets skip its intro. MIDI speed adjusts the notes to the recording while keeping the recording’s pitch and speed unchanged.

Sync audio & MIDI Find a match, then listen.

Find a starting point

Compare the recording’s attacks with your selected drum part. Analysis runs on this device. Use matching versions of the song.

Line up the notes and audio

Colored markers show the MIDI drum hits over the audio waveform. The rows below separate drums that strike together. Click a hit in a drum row to select its MIDI bar and beat, then click the matching audio peak and choose Apply beat match. Gold lines mark bar starts; the gold cursor is your chosen recording time.

Markers move with the current offset and MIDI speed. Use the 2-second window to align individual attacks more precisely.

Choose the same later beat in both files, preferably near the end. This fits one overall tempo difference; changing live tempo or different arrangements may need shorter practice sections.

Move mappings and sync settings to another computer. Bring the original MIDI and audio separately.

Publishing uploads this MIDI, recording, and sync setup to the shared school library. Every signed-in student can practice it.

Choose a MIDI file or try the sample song.

MAKE IT YOURS

Your drum controls.

Choose Change, then press a key. Add an alternate key for two-handed rolls. Enter starts a run; Esc stops it.

Changes save automatically on this device.

Leave delay correction at 0 to start. Positive values subtract device delay from measured hits. This is a manual adjustment, not an automatic calibration.

Match rate = hits ÷ (expected notes + extra hits). Timing averages use matched hits only. Opposite timing errors can cancel; average error shows their size.

BUILT FOR THE PRACTICE ROOM

A starting groove.

A browser prototype for Sierra Charter School. Original exercises and synthesized drum sounds; no downloads or accounts are needed for local practice.

Built with open source

Keyboard input and control ID helpers are adapted from SightKick by Anton Korolkov, under the MIT license. MIDI file decoding uses midi-file by Carter Thaxton (MIT license). The timing engine, sounds, exercises, and interface are new.

Next up

This version includes teacher/student accounts, shared school songs and saved progress when school storage is enabled. Local practice includes 24 original tracks, section repeats, drum focus, tempo building, sheet music for imported MIDI, and backing-audio sync tools. Match a beat or try a suggested alignment, then preview it before playing. Next: Roland TD-17 input when the kit is available. Keyboard and on-screen controls stay available.

Practice tips

Use wired headphones or speakers for timing practice. Some keyboards miss certain three-key combinations; change keys if a pad doesn’t light up. Touch input is useful for trying sounds; use the keyboard for timing assessment.
